subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What percentage of the total GCSE mark does Component 2: Performing Music contribute?
questions.explain: In AQA GCSE Music (8271), Component 2: Performing Music is worth 30% of the qualification.

questions.q: How is Component 2: Performing Music assessed?
options: A written examination set and marked by AQA
Non-exam assessment marked by the teacher and moderated by AQA
A listening exam marked by AQA
An oral exam conducted by a visiting AQA examiner
questions.explain: Performing is non-exam assessment (NEA), marked internally by the centre and moderated externally by AQA.

questions.q: How many separate performances must a student submit for Component 2?
options: One performance only
Two performances: one solo and one ensemble
Three performances of contrasting styles
Four performances across the two years
questions.explain: Candidates must submit two performances: one as a soloist and one as part of an ensemble.

questions.q: What is the minimum total duration required across both performances?
options: Two minutes
Four minutes
Six minutes
Eight minutes
questions.explain: The combined length of the solo and ensemble performances must be a minimum of four minutes.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration of the ensemble performance?
options: Thirty seconds
One minute
Two minutes
Three minutes
questions.explain: The ensemble performance must last for at least one minute within the four-minute total.

questions.q: At what standard (level of demand) are full marks available for a performance?
options: Grade 1
Grade 3
Grade 5
Grade 8
questions.explain: AQA sets Grade 3 standard as the level of demand at which full marks become available.

questions.q: In an ensemble performance, the candidate's individual part must:
options: Be doubled by another performer for support
Not be doubled by another performer
Always be the melody line
Be pre-recorded on a backing track
questions.explain: The candidate's part must be distinct and not doubled, so their individual contribution can be assessed.

questions.q: Why does playing along to a backing track NOT satisfy the ensemble requirement?
options: Backing tracks are banned in all performances
An ensemble requires interaction with at least one other live musician
Backing tracks make the performance too easy to mark
The ensemble must always be unaccompanied
questions.explain: An ensemble must involve the candidate interacting with one or more other live performers, which a backing track does not provide.

questions.q: What happens if a candidate performs a piece more difficult than Grade 3 standard?
options: They receive bonus marks above the maximum
Full marks remain available but no extra credit is given for the higher demand
Their marks are automatically capped
The performance is disqualified for being too hard
questions.explain: Performing above Grade 3 does not earn additional marks; full marks are simply available, with no penalty or bonus.

questions.q: What is the effect of performing a piece below Grade 3 standard?
options: It has no effect on the marks available
The marks available are capped below the maximum
The performance gains extra marks for accessibility
It must be re-recorded at a higher grade
questions.explain: A lower level of demand than Grade 3 limits the marks a candidate can achieve, even with an accurate performance.

questions.q: Which of these is a core aspect of accuracy assessed in a performance?
options: The correct pitch and rhythm of the notes played
The choice of concert venue
The cost of the instrument used
The number of audience members present
questions.explain: Accuracy is judged on how correctly the candidate reproduces the pitches and rhythms of the piece.

questions.q: Expression and interpretation in a performance are demonstrated mainly through:
options: Dynamics, phrasing and articulation
The length of the piece only
The genre of music chosen
The name of the composer
questions.explain: Interpretation is shown through musical elements such as dynamics, phrasing, articulation and appropriate tempo.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of musicians needed for a valid ensemble performance?
options: Two, including the candidate
One (the candidate alone)
Four musicians
Six musicians
questions.explain: An ensemble needs at least two performers, meaning the candidate plus at least one other live musician.

questions.q: A candidate performs a two-minute solo. To meet all requirements, how long must the ensemble performance be?
options: At least thirty seconds
At least one minute
At least two minutes
Exactly four minutes
questions.explain: The total must reach four minutes, so a two-minute solo requires an ensemble of at least two minutes (which also satisfies the one-minute minimum).

questions.q: A flautist plays an ensemble piece where a second flute plays exactly the same line throughout. Why is this a problem?
options: The piece is too long
The candidate's part is doubled, so their individual contribution cannot be assessed
Flutes are not allowed in ensembles
The ensemble has too many performers
questions.explain: Because the candidate's line is doubled, it cannot be distinguished and assessed independently, breaching the ensemble rules.

questions.q: A singer performs one piece accompanied by a pianist who follows the singer. How should this be classified?
options: An ensemble performance
A solo performance with accompaniment
An invalid performance
Both a solo and an ensemble at once
questions.explain: An accompanist supporting a featured performer counts as an accompanied solo, not an ensemble.

questions.q: A student wants to maximise marks in their solo. Which choice best supports this?
options: A piece at their secure Grade 3 standard played accurately and expressively
The hardest piece they can find, played with many wrong notes
A very easy piece played perfectly but well below Grade 3
The shortest possible piece to reduce the risk of errors
questions.explain: A Grade 3 piece performed accurately and expressively gives access to full marks without the errors that harder pieces risk.

questions.q: Which of the following is an acceptable means of performing for Component 2?
options: Only classical orchestral instruments
Any instrument or voice, including technology-based performance
Voice only, with no instruments permitted
Only instruments taught within the school
questions.explain: Candidates may perform on any instrument or voice, and technology-based performance routes are also permitted.

specSource: AQA GCSE Music (8271) specification; Component 2: Performing Music
